ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory proportionate, risk-based PEP identification (local law of 12 Nov 2004 art. 3-2), obligatory screening against EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List (non-exhaustive but customary), Belgian-Luxembourg Administrative List, and CSSF AML Guidance (18/698). Automated screening independently by the Luxembourg registered agent and notary; results logged and retained for a minimum of five years post-cessation of business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés), portal accessible at www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Luxembourgish, French, or German may be used for the name; Latin script mandatory. French transliteration controls for RCS registration. Names must comply with the Luxembourg Commercial Code and not violate public policy. Non-roman script names are not accepted; required to be romanized.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Investment Fund, Fonds, SICAV, SIF, Part II Fund
State, Government, National, Royal, Municipal, Communal
Luxembourg (geographic indication requiring prior authorization by the Minister of the Economy)
Supervision, Regulated, Recognized, Approved (implying public endorsement)
Stock Exchange, Clearing House, Settlement Institution
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 30 days of LBR rejection, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) at 6, Rue de la Rencontre, 7490 Luxembourg-Wecker. If rejected again, the appeal must be brought before the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg within three months of notification under the amended law of 7 November 1996 on the organization of the administrative courts. The appellant may also submit a curative name and re-file in a standard E5 RCS application. The initial rejection notice from LBR must be attached to any appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A full-time registered office within Luxembourg is mandatory. Pure 'virtual office' (mail-not-real-address) is unacceptable because the RCS requires an operational address where official documents can be served under art. 100 of the Luxembourg Commercial Code. However, a licensed corporate domiciliation agent may supply a qualifying administrative address, provided the SCSp maintains genuine economic substrate through its domiciliation agreement, which must include a contractually rent/use of the space and access to office support.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: RCS registrar annual random compliance check: ~2% probability. CSSF AML supervisory inspection for the selected GDP/pharma logistics activity: 8% (moderate risk segment). Luxembourg customs (Administration des douanes et accises) may perform unannounced premises visits when the entity holds a customs authorisation (e.g., AEOF) – 12% in the first two years post incorporation if traffic volumes exceed 5,000 shipments/year.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, in particular Articles 1-7 and Articles 198-213 (Société en Commandite Spéciale introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013), read with the Law of 19 December 2003 on the Register of Commerce and Companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés de Luxembourg (RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), filing exclusively via the gui'lettre e-filing portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Form A) submitted together with the executed limited partnership agreement (convention de société) on the gui'lettre portal, followed by publication in the RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SCSp has no statutory minimum subscribed capital; capital is freely fixed in the limited partnership agreement and may be paid in cash or in kind upon execution. No escrow account is required by the Law of 10 August 1915; voluntary escrow may be agreed between partners pending the GDP licensing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the undersigned execute the limited partnership agreement of SCSp and subscribe 1,000 partnership interests at €1 each, fully paid, credited as initial capital; (2) that the registered office of the SCSp be fixed at 2, boulevard de la Foire, L-1528 Luxembourg; (3) that the General Partner appoints [Name], as Gérant, with sole authority to represent the SCSp in all matters; (4) that the Gérant proceed with RCS, VAT, RBE, and social security registrations; (5) that the Gérant open bank accounts and apply for GDP distribution authorisation; (6) that all filings be executed. Unanimously adopted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Execution and Capital Subscription of the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Direct act of the General Partner(s) and Limited Partner(s); optional intervention of a Luxembourg notary if real estate is contributed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the convention de société identifying the general partner (unlimited liability) and limited partners, capital contributions, profit-sharing, management powers of the Gérant, and registered office. Execute by private deed (sous seing privé) unless notarization is voluntarily elected. Evidence the full payment of the subscribed capital into an account in the name of the SCSp or the Gérant.
required_dossiers: Executed limited partnership agreement (LPA)
Schedule of capital subscriptions and payment receipts
Identity documents of all partners and the appointed Gérant
Power of attorney for any signing agents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a partner challenges the terms, re-execute an amended LPA; if the RCS later flags the deed form, execute a notarial deed with retroactive effect permitted under article 2 of the 1915 Law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Incorporation Filing with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS Luxembourg via the gui'lettre portal (guilettre.lbr.lu) of Luxembourg Business Registers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form A (declaration pour immatriculation) electronically, attaching the executed LPA, the Gérant's mandate, and certification of the general partner's corporate existence if the GP is a legal person. Upload the RCS fee payment receipt and request immediate RESA publication upon registration.
required_dossiers: RCS Form A signed by the Gérant or authorised agent
Executed limited partnership agreement
Gérant's passport and proof of residence
Certificate of legal existence and excerpt of the GP corporate register
Power of attorney for the filing agent (notarially certified if non-Luxembourg resident)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or refusal, correct the form within the 15-day response period; re-submit via gui'lettre and, if refused, appeal to the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) under the Law of 19 December 2003.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT and Social Security Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the national registration number, Luxembourg VAT number (n° TVA) for the SCSp, and affiliation of the Gérant and personnel with the CCSS. Submit the RCS excerpt, LPA, and identification of the Gérant; elect for separate VAT identification of the SCSp despite its lack of legal personality.
required_dossiers: RCS incorporation excerpt (dated within 3 months)
Limited partnership agreement
AEDT VAT application form
CCSS affiliation questionnaire
Gérant and partner identity documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEDT queries the application, submit supplementary annexes requested under the VAT circular; appeal the assessment to the Directeur de l'AEDT within 3 months and subsequently to the administrative tribunal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial Ownership Registration and RESA Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs, RBE) administered by Luxembourg Business Registers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of RCS registration, file the RBE-1 form identifying all ultimate beneficial owners controlling the partners or the LPA, with supporting ownership scheme. Confirm automatic publication of the formation act in the RESA electronic compendium and monitor the publication date for use in subsequent permit applications.
required_dossiers: RBE-1 electronic form
Ownership and control structure chart
Identification documents of each beneficial owner
RCS excerpt confirming registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: RBE rejection is cure by refiling corrected UBO data within one month with evidence of the control chain; persistent non-filing exposes penalties of EUR 1,250 to EUR 1,250,000 plus publication of sanction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Establishment Permit (Autorisation d'établissement) for Freight and Logistics Activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Économie, Direction générale de l'industrie, filed through the Guichet.lu single window.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply under the Law of 2 September 2011 and Grand-Ducal Regulation of 28 July 2018 for the business permit covering ISIC 5229 freight forwarding and logistics support. Provide the Gérant's professional qualifications or proof of managerial experience in logistics, criminal record certificate, and evidence of compliant storage premises.
required_dossiers: Business establishment permit application via Guichet.lu
RCS excerpt
Gérant identity, residence permit and curriculum
Certificat judiciaire (good conduct certificate)
Diplomas or professional experience proof in transport operations
Lease title or property deed of the warehouse premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry requests additional evidence, respond within the granted delay to complete the file; a refusal may be appealed to the Administrative Tribunal within 3 months, supported by a certified equivalency of qualifications.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening with SWIFT and ACH-Equivalent Rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution authorized by the CSSF (Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a SCSp corporate account presenting the RCS excerpt, LPA, RBE filing, and the First Board Resolution listing signatories. Configure SWIFT wire capability and the local SEPA direct debit equivalent of Direct_ACH for collections; complete AML/KYC beneficial ownership declarations in line with the Law of 12 November 2004 on anti-money laundering.
required_dossiers: RCS excerpt
RBE acknowledgement
Limited partnership agreement
First board resolution and mandate of signatories
Business establishment permit or receipt of application
KYC/AML forms and source of funds declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If KYC is refused, supplement the source-of-funds documentation; escalate within the bank's internal review and, failing approval, engage an alternative CSSF-regulated bank or payment institution offering SWIFT and SEPA direct debit services.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction de la Pharmacie et des Médicaments, Ministère de la Santé, jointly with the Ministère de l'Économie for the business establishment permit.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Wholesale Distribution Authorization for Medicinal Products for Human Use (Autorisation de distribution en gros) issued under Luxembourg pharmacy law and EU GDP guidelines (2013/C 343/01), plus the business establishment permit for freight forwarding (commissionnaire de transport) under the Law of 2 September 2011.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Environmental Protection Agency of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Pharmaceutical freight warehouse typically falls under Class 4 (registration/declaration) of the Commodo-Incommodo classification (Grand-Ducal Regulation of 7 June 2002); a full EIA under the Law of 15 May 2018 is required only if the facility exceeds the category thresholds or is located in a Natura 2000 zone.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Sanitary wastewater must meet the discharge thresholds of the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 15 December 2009 before municipal sewer connection; no significant VOC point-source emissions expected; HVAC and cold-chain refrigerants must comply with EU F-Gas Regulation (EU) No 517/2014; all waste, including expired pharmaceuticals, must be collected by Administration de l'environnement-registered waste operators under the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance (avis de sécurité) from the Corps Grand-Ducal d'Incendie et de Secours (CGDIS) covering sprinkler protection, emergency exits and hazard zoning; structural load inspection certificates for racking, cold rooms and mezzanine floors; occupational safety and health approval from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering CE-marked material handling equipment, thermal stress controls for cold-chain staff, and a site-specific emergency plan.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; business registration administered by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR); all public procedures filed through the MyGuichet.lu portal (www.guichet.lu / myguichet.lu)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Notarize the SCSp partnership deed and register the partnership with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) via MyGuichet.lu to obtain the business registration number (matricule) and the entity national identification number. Step 2: Submit the VAT registration application (Formulaire 645) to the AEDT through the MyGuichet.lu/eTVA portal, attaching the partnership deed, identification of the general partner (associé gérant), proof of the Luxembourg registered office, and the GDP logistics/premium-freight activity description. Step 3: Obtain the LU VAT identification number (format LU + 8 digits) issued by the AEDT. Step 4: Apply for an EORI number for customs export/import declarations. Step 5: File any social security registrations with the Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS) where the SCSp engages employees or a gérant assimilé.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SCSp is a fiscally transparent partnership without legal personality; no entity-level corporate income tax (CIT) or municipal business tax (MBT) is imposed and taxable items flow through to the partners. Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime; however, the transparent SCSp may be recharacterized as opaque under the ATAD hybrid-mismatch rules (Law of 26 July 2019) where a mismatch produces a deduction/non-inclusion or double-deduction outcome. For VAT, the SCSp may register as a taxable person where it performs an independent economic activity, and the general partner acts as statutory representative. The SCSp may elect quarterly or annual VAT return filing based on prior-year turnover and may apply to the AEDT for a cash-accounting scheme or for fixed-establishment treatment where a local establishment exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: The Article 57 VAT-Law small-business franchise exemption applies at EUR 35,000 annual turnover for goods and EUR 25,000 for service activities. International freight forwarding, transport arrangement and GDP logistics (ISIC 5229) supplied on a B2B basis fall under the general place-of-supply rule (customer establishment) with reverse charge, and no domestic VAT registration threshold applies to a non-resident supplier of such cross-border services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, API reporting or digital stamping for B2B e-invoicing. Mandatory B2G e-invoicing applies since March 2021 in the PEPPOL Peppol BIS 3.0 format. B2B pharma-freight invoices may be issued electronically (EDI/UBL/PDF) subject to the authenticity, integrity and legibility requirements of Articles 58-60 of the VAT Law, with a 10-year retention obligation; no QR-code or cross-border clearance transmission is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to (i) supplies of goods physically exported outside the EU (Article 155 of the VAT Law) and (ii) transport services directly related to such exported goods, provided the export is effected within 90 days of supply (extendable to 150 days upon justified AEDT authorization) and evidenced by prescribed documentation. For B2B freight-forwarding and customs-brokerage services linked to pharma imports/exports, the reverse-charge mechanism applies within the EU; services relating to non-EU transportation are zero-rated or outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT. Zero-rating requires the supplier to hold positive legal evidence of physical exit from EU customs territory, including the electronic customs export declaration, the bill of lading or CMR/air waybill, counterparty acceptance, and, for GDP pharma cargo, the unbroken cold-chain/temperature-excursion log and reconciliation with the Export Accompanying Document (EAD) where applicable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD - Single Administrative Document, electronic customs declaration and, where applicable, Export Accompanying Document/EAD evidencing physical exit from EU territory)
Bill of Lading (sea) or CMR / IATA Air Waybill and aircraft or vessel manifest (air/road)
Inward Remittance Certificate and bank SWIFT credit confirmation evidencing receipt of foreign currency export proceeds
Commercial invoice, packing list and freight agreement containing the GDP pharma reference and Incoterms 2020 allocation
Signed proof of delivery (POD) / consignee certificate of receipt together with the GDP temperature excursion log and chain-of-custody records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg statutory law does not impose a monetary FX-repatriation deadline; the 180-day benchmark reflects the customary AEDT documentary-verification horizon and EU export-proof standards. Where export zero-rating is claimed without the required customs and transport evidence, the AEDT reclassifies the supply as taxable at 17%, assesses under-declared VAT, and applies late-payment interest of 0.8% per month (Article 66 of the VAT Law); deduction rights may also be restricted or excluded. Knowingly false declarations or simulated physical export expose the taxable person to criminal sanctions under Article 78 of the VAT Law (imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years and/or a criminal fine of up to EUR 250,000), administrative fines of up to EUR 4,000 per infraction, retrospective clawback of VAT and interest, and publication of the sanction; AEDT criminal-referral practice is consistent for sham pharma-freight export schemes.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), functioning within the European System of Central Banks (ESCB) and subject to EU Treaties on capital movements and payments
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a full member of the euro area and maintains no foreign-exchange controls. Both current and capital account transactions are freely convertible and transferable under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. The Luxembourg franc was fully replaced by the euro and no convertibility restriction applies to profit remittances, capital repatriation, or current trade payments. For an SCSp, distributions to non-resident partners are generally permitted, but banks must verify the partnership agreement, beneficial ownership registers, and applicable EU/UN sanctions and anti-money-laundering compliance. A profit-remittance transaction is not subject to the CSSF or BCL approval, but must be documented to satisfy the counterparty bank's internal controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg has no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, no minimum conversion ratio, and no mandatory repatriation deadline for export or freight receipts. Export invoices may be paid in any foreign currency and may be retained in offshore or onshore accounts at the commercial discretion of the SCSp, subject only to EU/UN sanctions and AML/KYC obligations. Where the business generates freight revenue in USD, conversion to EUR is at the prevailing market rate via a licensed Luxembourg bank or passported EEA financial institution.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (EUR) and Operational Current Account (EUR/USD)
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Multi-Currency Account (EUR/USD/GBP)
Operational Current Account and Corporate FX Settlement Account (EUR/USD)
Operational Current Account and Wealth-Structure Escrow Account (EUR)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-Limited. An EEA-licensed Electronic Money Institution or Payment Institution may passport into Luxembourg under the Second Payment Services Directive (PSD2) and may provide ancillary cross-border payment accounts. However, offshore non-EEA digital EMIs are not legally permitted to provide payment services in Luxembourg without a licence or passport. For an SCSp involved in GDP pharmaceutical freight, the primary treasury, capital escrow, and FX settlement accounts must be held with CSSF-regulated credit institutions or authorised EEA branches. A regulated EEA EMI may be used only for operational liquidity in euros where low-value supplier disbursements are made and no import/export financing is required.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person or substantially equivalent identity verification is generally required for the general partner and the ultimate beneficial owners of the SCSp. Most Luxembourg banks mandate at least one physical KYC meeting with the authorised signatory or the appointed local administrative agent. Remote opening may be accepted where a bank operates a CSSF-approved electronic onboarding workflow and the structure qualifies as low-risk; in practice, the corporate register extract, notarised partnership agreement excerpt, valid ID documents, proof of physical address, and a board resolution authorising the account are required. Remote attestation, apostilled documents, and existing-bank reference letters may reduce interview burden but do not eliminate it.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The SCSp has a multi-layered corporate ownership chain, including a non-resident general partner or discretionary-managed investor
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Onboarding file containing: consolidated ownership and control chart identifying all ultimate beneficial owners; notarised and apostilled partnership agreement or LPA extract explicitly granting account-opening authority; certificate of registered office and good standing from the Luxembourg Regifleet/RCS and foreign registry; valid passports and utility bills for all UBOs; source-of-wealth declarations and recent bank references.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No employees, physical office, or demonstrable local substance in Luxembourg despite the SCSp conducting GDP logistics trade
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Services agreement with a licensed Luxembourg corporate domiciliation agent; lease or service-office contract; registered address certificate from the Luxembourg Trade Register; appointment deed for a local general partner or authorised local manager; Luxembourg VAT registration certificate; annual accounts or draft financial statements confirming actual transaction flow; professional indemnity insurance certification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pharmaceutical and GDP freight activity triggers high-scrutiny reviews around product classification, controlled goods, and supply-chain transparency
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg or EU GDP wholesale distribution licence / certification; temperature-controlled logistics standard operating procedures (SOPs); signed client and sub-carrier contracts; commercial invoice, packing list, air/sea waybill with HS Code 5229/488510 reference; valid pharma importer/exporter licences of counterparties; medical device or drug transport insurance certificate; customs broker appointment letter for arriving shipments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large and irregular inbound capital contributions from non-EU investors, triggering source of funds and sanctions screening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed capital call notices and subscription agreements; original bank SWIFT reference from contributing investors; three months of investor account statements showing lawful accumulation; tax and wealth statements; audited financial statements or independent accountant letters from the investing counterparty; formal anti-money-laundering and sanctions certification from the sending bank; board minutes approving the capital injection.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Investment capital for the SCSp must enter via an international wire transfer using SWIFT MT103 from the investor's bank to the Luxembourg escrow or operating account. The payment message should include an ISO 20022 or treasury purpose classification consistent with a direct capital contribution, typically structured as a general remittance or equity capital movement under the EU Capital Movements Directive, and the remittance information field must identify the SCSp name, the capital call number, and the contributing partner. The receiving bank will require the capital call statement, contribution agreement, and partner register extract to classify the wire as equity rather than taxable debt or services income. If the inflow originates from a non-EU jurisdiction, additional economic sanctions clearance and a legal opinion on EU capital-movement compliance may be required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: EUR-denominated outbound payments to freight forwarders, warehouses, customs brokers, and insurance providers are cleared through SEPA Credit Transfer or instant SEPA Credit Transfer with structured remittance containing invoice number and purchase order reference. Non-EUR payments to international logistics counterparties are settled through SWIFT MT103 messages across the relevant correspondent network (e.g., USD through a US correspondent bank). For high-value pharmaceutical freight or controlled-temperature equipment procurement, an irrevocable documentary Commercial Letter of Credit may be used to ensure title and logistics documents are exchanged against payment, particularly when the supplier demands assurance of payment before dispatch. All clearing rails must enforce EU sanctions screening, anti-money-laundering pending-transaction monitoring, and goods-level export-control checks.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable Outright FX Forward (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF)
Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) on emerging-market or restricted currencies
FX Swap (spot leg plus forward leg)
Cross-Currency Swap (EUR/USD basis or fixed-floating structural hedging)
Plain Vanilla FX Options and FX Collar structures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within one month following the approval of annual accounts, or, where no accounts are required, annually by 31 December; exact date set by RCS renewal notice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties up to EUR 5,000; repeated non-compliance may lead to administrative strike-off and judicial dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual accounts with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after the end of the financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-imposed fines up to EUR 10,000 per general partner; risk of civil liability and administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return for a taxable SCSp
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within nine months after the end of the tax year; generally due 31 March for calendar-year taxpayers unless extended
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default surcharge of 10% on outstanding tax; late payment interest of 0.6% per month; criminal fines for repeated failure to file

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual net wealth tax return for a taxable SCSp
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with the annual corporate income tax return, within nine months after the end of the tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10%; monthly interest at 0.6%; coercive recovery through tax enforcement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual value-added tax return for Luxembourg VAT registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual VAT return due no later than the last working day of April of the following calendar year; monthly or quarterly returns for certain taxpayers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty up to EUR 10,000; late payment interest at 0.6% per month; criminal sanctions for intentional non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of registered office, registered agent and statutory registers with the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually at the anniversary of the RCS registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 5,000; failure to confirm may trigger administrative dissolution

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for any Luxembourg undertaking, including an SCSp, if it exceeds at least two of three criteria: balance sheet total exceeding EUR 4,400,000; net turnover exceeding EUR 8,800,000; average number of employees exceeding 50. Audit also mandated if all general partners are corporate entities or if consolidated accounts are prepared.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP aligned with EU Fourth Directive; IFRS permitted and often preferred for consolidated accounts

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually the SCSp must confirm to the RCS that the Register of Beneficial Owners is complete and accurate; any transfer of partnership interests must be reported to the RBE within one month of the transaction, with annual confirmation transmitted via the Luxembourg Business Registers online portal
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 - 3,500 annually for a Luxembourg registered office and corporate agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - 15,000 for a simple SCSp statutory audit, higher for consolidated groups

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at SCSp level (fiscally transparent hybrid partnership); 24.94% combined Luxembourg City headline rate for FY2024 if the SCSp exercises the corporate tax opting-in election (17% corporate income tax + 1.19% solidarity employment fund surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax on Luxembourg City multiplier 2.25).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP Box: 80% exemption on qualifying intellectual property income, yielding an effective CIT rate of approximately 4.99% (24.94% x 20%). Participation exemption: 0% CIT on qualifying dividend income and capital gains where a >=10% participation or >=EUR 1.2m acquisition cost is held >=12 months and the 2024 substance/anti-abuse test is satisfied. Non-opted-in SCSp: no Luxembourg income tax, municipal business tax, or net wealth tax at the entity level as profits/losses flow through pro rata to partners; minimum net wealth tax of EUR 535 applies only to opted-in corporate entities.
corporate_income_tax_regime.loss_carryforward_description: Luxembourg law (Art. 110 LIR) permits indefinite carryforward of tax-deductible losses, with no statutory expiry for corporate taxpayers; for a transparent SCSp carried at partner level, loss utilization is subject to partner-specific pro rata allocation and substance/profit-intent anti-abuse review.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 800 (annual informational return for fiscally transparent partnerships, including SCSp) filed electronically via ACD eCDF portal (accessible through guichet.lu / MyGuichet). This form is not a CIT computation return; it reconciles the SCSp's income allocation, partner register, capital movements, and general partner remuneration.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Must be filed by 31 December of the calendar year immediately following the fiscal year-end (Art. 162 LIR); for a 31 December 2024 year-end, statutory due date is 31 December 2025. Additional grace periods are administrative-only and require a justified written request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, RCS registration number, Luxembourg business address, fiscal year start/end dates, main activity (ISIC 5229 / GDP pharma freight forwarding), and status of the general partner (commandité) and limited partners (commanditaires).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the non-resident partner's full name, country of tax residence, Luxembourg tax identification number (if any), and percentage of partnership interests; do not report Luxembourg-source income of passive non-resident limited partners unless a Luxembourg permanent establishment exists or commercial activity is exercised through the Luxembourg GP.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section II – Profit and Loss Allocation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable result computed under Luxembourg accounting rules (bilan/exploitation), split between general partner and limited partners according to the limited partnership agreement; includes service fees, freight revenue, cost of goods, depreciation, and interest expense on related-party financing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate partner: report only the allocable share attributable to a Luxembourg PE under Art. 2 LIR; treaty-capable income should be excluded if no PE exists; a non-resident limited partner with no active management role is generally not subject to Luxembourg income tax on the allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section III – Partner Remuneration and Loan-Back Interest
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report any management fees, carried-interest allocations, shareholder loans, interest paid to partners, and transactions with associated enterprises; such items are subject to Luxembourg Transfer Pricing rules (arm's length test).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners receiving management fees or interest from a Luxembourg SCSp must assess Luxembourg source taxation; treaty relief (e.g., EUR 0% interest article) requires a valid residence certificate and economic-beneficial-owner statement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section IV – Participation Schedule and Exemption Claims
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detail of participations held by the SCSp in underlying companies (name, registered office, shareholding percentage, acquisition cost, dividend/capital gain amounts claimed under the participation exemption, and evidence of the underlying company's taxable status).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners cannot directly claim the Luxembourg participation exemption on income from the SCSp; the exemption is applied at the SCSp/GP level only for the taxable corporate partner. Provide treaty article reference where the non-resident partner relies on a DTA tie-breaker or PE credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section V – Substantiation of Substance (2024 Anti-Abuse Filing)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of economic substance: number of qualified employees in Luxembourg, local premises, actual decision-making (board minutes), bank accounts operated in Luxembourg, and commercial rationale for GDP freight operations; required for the exemption claims and to pre-empt Art. 168ter LIR recharacterization.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident limited partners must certify that no artificial arrangement exists; if the SCSp is deemed a shell without substance, the partners may be subject to reclassification, withheld-tax reassessments, and penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section VI – DTAs and Foreign PE Declarations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of foreign branches or permanent establishments, foreign taxes paid, and claim of applicable DTA tax credits or exemptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a copy of the TRC for each non-resident partner; request treaty credit for foreign-source income allocated to them; only income connected to the Luxembourg PE is taxable in Luxembourg.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a default assessment plus monthly late-payment interest of 0.6% per commenced month (Art. 155 LIR); administrative fine of EUR 250 to EUR 4,000 per missing return (Art. 174 LIR); where under-declaration stems from wilful concealment, an additional tax surcharge of 10% to 75% of the evaded tax applies, and criminal prosecution may follow (Art. 180 LIR).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 700 (unified annual CIT, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax return) filed electronically via ACD eCDF portal only where the SCSp has made a valid corporate taxation opting-in election, converting the entity into a taxable Luxembourg company.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: By 31 December of the year following the fiscal year-end (Art. 162 LIR); extension requests are assessed case-by-case; taxable assessment remains provisional until formal notice of assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate name, registered office, RCS number, activity code (ISIC 5229), fiscal year, and election reference confirming the SCSp's opted-in status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident partner, attach a copy of the partnership agreement and the election election form; note that the opting-in applies entity-wide and binds all partners.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corrected net profit per Luxembourg GAAP, including provisions, depreciation, foreign exchange gains, and disallowed expenses (non-deductible VAT, fines, excessive interest, and royalties on related-party IP payments).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners may notionally claim the same commercial result for treaty credit purposes; Luxembourg-source income taxable in Luxembourg only to the extent effectively connected with the opted-in entity's PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box C – Taxable Base and Loss Carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter current-year taxable income or loss after adjustments; apply the indefinite loss carryforward (Art. 110 LIR); state the 80% IP deduction and any notional interest deduction or investment tax credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate partner claiming indirect foreign tax credit must obtain a statement of the Luxembourg taxable base and CIT paid from the SCSp.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box D – Municipal Business Tax (ICC) Calculation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Separately compute municipal business tax base (reduced by the applicable allowance) and apply the Luxembourg City multiplier.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Municipal business tax is not creditable in all residence states; analyze the DTA business-profits or other-income article.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box E – Dividends and Capital Gains Exemption
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List qualifying participation dividends and capital gains to be excluded under Arts. 147 and 166 LIR and verify each subsidiary's taxable status and the 12-month holding condition.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where dividends would flow to a non-resident partner, reduction of the 15% WHT to 0% requires TRC, ownership-history declaration, and proof of the anti-abuse substance test.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile Luxembourg dividends WHT (15% or 0%), interest WHT (0%), and royalties WHT (0%) applied during the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For treaty relief at source, the paying entity must hold the partner's TRC and a completed beneficial-owner statement before reducing the WHT; otherwise, claim a refund through the Luxembourg direct tax office.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: monthly late-payment interest of 0.6% and administrative fine of EUR 250 to EUR 4,000; failure to pay the assessed tax triggers a 10% automatic increase on the due tax (Art. 166 LIR regulation) and interest as above; a fraudulent return exposes the taxpayer to an additional surcharge of up to 75% and criminal sanctions under Art. 180 LIR.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for a transparent SCSp because profit allocations to partners are not legally 'dividends' and no Luxembourg withholding obligation arises at the SCSp level. If the SCSp has opted into CIT, the statutory dividend WHT is 15% (Art. 149 LIR), reduced to 0% under the participation exemption (holding >=10% or acquisition price >=EUR 1.2m held >=12 months) and under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (subject to the 2024 substance and anti-abuse verification).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: STEP 1: The paying Luxembourg entity (or the SCSp in opted-in cases) collects from the non-resident partner/beneficial owner: (i) an official tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the residence state's tax authority; (ii) a completed beneficial-owner declaration (Luxembourg ACD form type 'attestation de résidence fiscale' plus dividend/interest ownership statement); (iii) proof of shareholding and holding period (register extracts, subscription agreements, bank transfers). STEP 2: Apply the DTA rate at source (commonly 5% or 0% for >=10% shareholders; 0% interest and royalties under the 2009 Luxembourg-US protocol and most modern DTAs). STEP 3: Where the reduced rate cannot be applied at source, submit a reclaim to the Luxembourg RTS (Service des Renseignements) attaching the return, TRC, and underlying documentation. STEP 4: Maintain a full audit file of all TRCs, ownership back-to-back contracts, and substance evidence for at least 6 years, as the 2024 anti-abuse rules (Art. 168ter LIR) require the ultimate beneficial owner’s economic substance to be demonstrated.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: Luxembourg does not levy withholding tax on arm's length interest paid to non-residents (domestic statutory rate 0%); treaty rate is also 0% under the Luxembourg-US treaty (2009 protocol) and most Luxembourg DTAs. Royalties: Luxembourg abolished its royalty WHT as from 1 January 2004; statutory domestic rate is 0% on IP royalties paid to non-residents; under most DTAs the rate is 0% (e.g., US treaty 0%). Caution: royalty payments to related parties are deductible only if economically justified, and excessive or abusive IP payments may be disallowed or recharacterized as a distribution (which would then trigger 15% dividend WHT absent participation exemption).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 450,000 in annual cross-border transactions with associated enterprises triggers the mandatory Local File requirement (Circular LIR n°56/1 of 28 January 2022, derived from EU TPD). A Master File is required where the worldwide group's consolidated turnover equals or exceeds EUR 50 million. Transactions below EUR 450,000 may still require simplified documentation on request; all intercompany transactions must be at arm's length regardless of documentation threshold.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Appraisal / Valuation of Intangibles under OECD Chapter VI where applicable
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies an anti-abuse substance doctrine through (i) the statutory GAAR in Art. 6 of the General Tax Law (LGI/Steueranpassungsgesetz of 30 October 1934) codifying the 'abus de droit' principle; (ii) the 2024 Budget Law (loi du 29 mars 2024) inserting Art. 168ter LIR requiring substantive economic activity – adequate premises, qualified staff, actual management, and genuine business rationale – to benefit from the participation exemption, the dividend WHT exemption, and interest/royalty deduction rules; (iii) EU ATAD and the pending Unshell directive negotiation, under which shell entities without minimal substance can be denied tax benefits; and (iv) the Luxembourg administrative practice for SCSp partnerships which rejects artificial back-to-back structures lacking substance. A GDP pharma freight SCSp with nominal substance may be recharacterized as a taxable Luxembourg company, triggering CIT at 24.94%, reclassification of distributions as dividends subject to 15% WHT, and backdated penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly supplying false information on Form 800/700, omission of Luxembourg-source income, wilful concealment of a Luxembourg permanent establishment, falsified partner allocation, or use of a sham invoice flow to artificially reduce the taxable base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Art. 180 LIR: imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years and a fine of up to EUR 25,000; mandatory publication of the judgment; tax surcharge of 10% to 75% of the evaded tax; monthly late-payment interest of 0.6%; retention of the normal 10-year statute of limitation for fraud cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner of the SCSp (whether individual or corporate) is jointly and severally liable without limitation for the partnership's obligations; a corporate GP's directors may face civil restitution, disqualification, and, in aggravated cases, travel bans or imprisonment for complicity in fiscal fraud; the tax administration may pierce the veil where the GP is a mere shell.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell / Artificial SCSp Structure (Abus de Droit and 2024 Substance Rules)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an SCSp with no real commercial activity, no Luxembourg employees, no local management, and relying on a third-party administrator to conduct the entire GDP freight business, solely to exploit treaty eligibility or pass-through tax status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization as a fully taxable Luxembourg corporate entity; imposition of 24.94% CIT and municipal business tax on all profits recast retroactively; denial of the participation exemption and reimposition of 15% dividend WHT on all outbound distributions; additional penalties up to 75% and interest at 0.6% per month.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Art. 6 LGI and civil jurisprudence, directors of the corporate general partner who knowingly orchestrated the artificial structure are personally liable for the undercollected corporate tax and may be ordered to pay restitution; criminal courts may issue travel restrictions for non-resident directors and order imprisonment for up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare and maintain a Local File where cross-border related-party transactions exceed EUR 450,000; failure to file the Master File for groups with >=EUR 50 million revenue; absence of comparability analysis or arm's length benchmarking for management fees, interest, and royalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine of EUR 250 to EUR 4,000 per missing document; the tax administration may issue an estimated assessment with no burden of proof on the taxpayer; disallowance of the related-party deduction; penalty interest of 0.6% per month on the recomputed tax; possible voluntary disclosure limitations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed the acknowledgment that no documentation exists may be held jointly liable for the assessed tax in the event of the entity's insolvency; in flagrant cases, personal fines are imposed under the general shareholder/manager liability provisions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file and keep current the beneficial ownership information in the Luxembourg Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE); failure to identify ultimate individual owners behind the SCSp's partners; lack of appropriate KYC and ongoing due diligence on the GDP pharma cargo financing flows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine of EUR 250 to EUR 1,250,000 for companies under the Luxembourg AML Law of 12 November 2004 (as amended) and the Law of 13 January 2019 on the RBE; delisting from commercial register; possible freezing of bank accounts and prohibition on payment rails (SWIFT/ACH).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner's directors face personal criminal liability with imprisonment of 3 months to 5 years for serious AML breaches; directors of corporate partners are jointly liable for the RBE filing obligation; travel bans and professional disqualifications are routinely ordered in significant cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Cross-Border Withholding Tax Abuses / Dividend Stripping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Engineering dividend allocations to a non-resident partner that has no economic ownership of the participation (nominee/share-lending), claiming treaty WHT relief without TRC or without beneficial ownership, or paying dividends to a jurisdiction with no DTA during the 12-month holding period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re imposition of the 15% domestic dividend WHT with a 25% surcharge; disallowance of the participation exemption; retroactive interest and penalties; in treaty-shopping cases, denial of treaty benefits and additional fines up to 75% of the avoided WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved the misuse of treaty relief can be made personally liable for the withholding tax shortfall, face civil fraud damages, and be subject to criminal prosecution with imprisonment up to 5 years; overseas travel restrictions may be imposed pending examination.
